messages:

Subject: Azure Private Plan - invoice routing & SLA exception request (Aurelius Pharma)

Hi Amanda —

Great speaking earlier. As discussed, I’ve attached the Redwood Azure Private Plan commercial term sheet for Aurelius (summary + standard private offer language). A few items I wanted to flag for procurement so we can get this into your procurement stack: 

- Invoice routing: Redwood invoices Azure via marketplace merchant flow by default. If you need vendor-billed PO route (your AP team prefers that), we can accommodate but it requires a short finance setup (merchant onboarding).
- Net payment terms: standard is net30 on marketplace settlements. You asked about net60; happy to discuss as an exception but we’ll need internal approvals.
- SLA credits & uptime: our standard marketplace SLA is 99.9% with available credits in section 4. Aurelius is asking for a higher uptime guarantee / extended credit cap — we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

Attached: Redwood_PrivatePlan_Terms_v1.pdf and SOW stub for the initial integration. Can you confirm the legal contact who will be sending redlines and whether Aurelius requires A4-formatted contract exhibits?

Next step: If you can send procurement redlines (or point me to the DocuSign request) I’ll loop in Legal and Finance to speed approvals.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Azure Private Plan - invoice routing & SLA exception request (Aurelius Pharma)

Sean,

Thanks for sending — our procurement and legal teams reviewed the term sheet. We have three asks up front: 

1) Invoice terms: Aurelius requires vendor-billed invoices (not marketplace merchant) with net60 payment terms. Without vendor-billed invoices, our ERP can’t process the PO.
2) SLA: We need a 99.95% uptime commitment for the production model used in regulated workloads, with credits capped at 50% of monthly fees.
3) Data residency & audit: please confirm logs retention and whether Redwood will provide CSV exports for audit evidence on request.

I’ve attached our redlines (Aurelius_Redlines_20261113.docx). Can Redwood turn these around by Monday 11/16? We are targeting procurement sign-off the week of 11/22 to align with our Q4 implementation window.

Best,
Amanda Lewis
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Aurelius Pharma
amanda.lewis@aureliuspharma.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Azure Private Plan - invoice routing & SLA exception request (Aurelius Pharma)

Looping in Karthik to check on commercial impact. Quick thoughts:

- Net60 & vendor-billed: finance will push back on net60 for marketplace merchant flows. If Aurelius absolutely needs vendor-billed, we can propose a hybrid: initial 3 months vendor-billed (to satisfy ERP) then move to marketplace merchant with standard net30. That gives finance a runway and avoids a permanent billing exposure.
- SLA: 99.95% is a stretch for our default private-plan offering. We might accept a targeted SLA on a per-model basis if they commit to a minimum monthly commit and agree to a higher credit cap in our commercial exhibits.
- Data residency: legal will confirm log export cadence; engineering already supports CSV exports for audit.

Can you ask Amanda if Aurelius is willing to commit to a minimum monthly spend (e.g., $75k/mo) in exchange for the higher SLA and net60 vendor-billed invoice path? If they will, we can fast-track approvals.

-M
Marissa Cole
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Azure Private Plan - invoice routing & SLA exception request (Aurelius Pharma)

Amanda —

Thanks for the redlines. Quick internal update: finance is open to a short vendor-billed onboarding (first 90 days) to allow your ERP to process the PO, after which we’d transition to the Azure marketplace merchant settlement. In parallel, Marissa is evaluating a higher SLA in exchange for a committed minimums clause.

Would Aurelius consider: 
- 90-day vendor-billed onboarding, net60 for those first invoices, then move to marketplace (net30) thereafter?
- A 12-month minimum committed spend at $75k/month to qualify for a targeted 99.95% SLA on the production model, with credits capped at 50% of monthly fees (as you requested).

If that sounds reasonable I’ll flag this for Legal (Karthik) to draft a short amendment and we’ll attach the DocuSign. If not, please propose an alternative.

Regards,
Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Azure Private Plan - invoice routing & SLA exception request (Aurelius Pharma)

Amanda / team —

I reviewed Aurelius’ redlines. We can accommodate the 90-day vendor-billed onboarding + net60 for those invoices. I’ll prepare a one-page amendment that: (1) documents the 90-day vendor-billed period and subsequent transition to marketplace settlement, (2) adds a commercial exhibit for the $75k/mo 12-month commit that upgrades the SLA to 99.95% for the specified production model, and (3) clarifies logs/exports cadence (engineering will provide weekly CSV exports for audit on request).

Two legal notes: 
- The SLA upgrade will include a standard carve-out for scheduled maintenance and force majeure; credits remain capped at 50% of monthly fees as a negotiated exception.
- Any permanent change to invoicing beyond the 90-day onboarding requires senior finance signoff (we’ve scoped this as an exception, not a new standard).

Amanda, I’ll send the amendment and commercial exhibit via DocuSign by EOD tomorrow so your procurement can review. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Agreements
Redwood Inference
